correctness.rationale: On chart with columns 2,4 independent, use invertible row operations to matrix N=[[-a,1,-(1+c),0],[-b,0,-d,1],[y,0,-x,0]]. Its signed maximal minors (x, a x+(1+c)y, y, b x+d y) satisfy Np=0 and Segre equation p0p3-p1p2=b x²+(d-a)xy-(1+c)y² exactly. In char2 derivatives with respect to a,b,c,d,x,y give xy,x²,y²,xy,(d-a)y,(d-a)x; as H belongs to (x²,xy,y²), singular Jacobian ideal is J=(x²,xy,y²,(d-a)x,(d-a)y). Localizing t=d-a invertible yields reduced (x,y). Holding tangency base t=0 gives three-dimensional Artin quotient k[x,y]/(x,y)², while odd characteristic tangent quadratic with nonzero square coefficient gives k[x]/(x²), length 2. At generic char2 t=0 with b and 1+c units, contact square root (1+c)/b is not a rational square since b has odd discrete valuation, so a purely inseparable degree-two field extension. Independent SymPy determinant/partial derivative rederivation matches identity; algebra/valuation, not finite random tests, covers the chart.
